topics.description: Vasco da Gama was a Portuguese explorer who led the first European voyage by sea from Europe to India in 1497–1498.
aliases: Vasco da Gama, 1st Count of Vidigueira

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer the following questions about Bartholomeu Dias.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Dias was an explorer for this country, for whom he sailed to regions such as modern day Namibia and Angola. Another explorer from this country, Pedro Cabral, was the European discoverer of Brazil.

parts.label: B
parts.question: On his way back from a voyage, Dias discovered and rounded this cape on the southern tip of Africa. Dias gave this cape the name “Cape of Storms,” though John II later gave it a more optimistic name.
parts.answer: Cape of Good Hope [prompt on the Cape]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Though Dias wanted to continue his voyage to the Indian Ocean, his crewmates unanimously voted to return to Portugal. This explorer later completed the full voyage, becoming the first European to reach India by sea.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country’s namesake empire fought a protracted war with the Adal Sultanate in the mid-16th century. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this country in the Horn of Africa where that Christian empire was ruled for 700 years by the Solomonic dynasty. This country’s final ruler, Haile Selassie, ruled from its capital of Addis Ababa until 1974.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Ethiopia [accept Abyssinia or the Ethiopian Empire or the Abyssinian Empire]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Ethiopia was nearly defeated by Adal before soldiers from this empire pushed back the invaders. This empire’s naval rivalry with the Ottoman Empire led them to support Ethiopia against the Ottoman-backed Adal Sultanate.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Portugal [or Kingdom of Portugal or Reino de Portugal; accept Portuguese Empire]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The commander of the Portuguese force in Ethiopia, Cristovaõ, was the son of this explorer. This explorer had earlier asked for trade concessions from the Zamorin of Calicut during his first expedition to India.

topics.description: The early 19th-century founder and first ruler of the Zulu Kingdom, known for reorganizing the Zulu military and expanding Zulu territory in southern Africa.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The last king of this ethnic group, Cetshwayo kaMpande (thet-shwah-yo kaam-paan-day), was defeated by a colonial army. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this ethnic group, which today is the largest in South Africa. A province of South Africa is named for this ethnic group and Natal.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This early 19th century Zulu monarch developed the "bull horn" formation and a shorter style of spear as part of his massive military reformation. The expansion of his realm is argued to have triggered the Mfecane (m-fay-thaa-nay), a long period of social upheaval in southern Africa.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The Zulu Kingdom was eventually defeated by this colonial power, whose armies were also involved in the Boer Wars in South Africa. This country's colonial possessions also included Nigeria, Canada, and Australia.
parts.answer: the British Empire [or the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, or the UK, or Great Britain]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This kingdom’s first ruler defeated a rival at the Battle of Gqokli (“ko-KLEE”) Hill despite being outnumbered two-to-one. This kingdom’s forces lost over three thousand soldiers after a failed assault on a fortified wagon train in the Battle of Blood River. The rise of this kingdom fueled a period of forced migration known as the (*) Mfecane. This kingdom frequently employed a battle tactic known as the “buffalo horn” formation. Despite winning a battle at Isandlwana, this kingdom’s ruler Cetshwayo was defeated in a war that ended with the capture of this kingdom’s capital of Ulundi. For 10 points, name this kingdom in modern-day South Africa founded by Shaka.

topics.description: A South American country on the Caribbean coast, known for its petroleum resources, Lake Maracaibo, and significant modern political history.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Fourteenth of June Movement was founded in this country by a group of activists nicknamed “Las Mariposas.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this country where those activists, the Mirabal sisters, opposed the dictatorship of Rafael Trujillo (“RA-FA-yell true-HI-yo”) in 1960 until their assassination in November of that year.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Trujillo earlier attempted to assassinate this South American country’s president Romulo Betancourt (“ROM-yu-low BET-ahn-core”) over Betancourt’s association with his opponents. This country’s later president Carlos Andrés Pérez was the target of a failed coup in 1992.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Trujillo’s own assassination in 1961 was aided by this US government agency while it was led by Allen Dulles. This organization is primarily focused on overseas espionage, unlike its domestic counterpart, the FBI.

topics.description: Philip II was the Habsburg king of Spain from 1556 to 1598, associated with Mary I of England and the Spanish Armada's attempted invasion of England.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A work named after this body of water analyzes it through three levels of time. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this large sea, which was studied through a longue durée approach by Fernand Braudel. Historical polities in northern Africa and southern Europe had a coastline on this sea.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Fernand Braudel’s Mediterranean is primarily focused during the reign of this Spanish monarch, who sent the Spanish Armada to invade England.
parts.answer: Philip II of Spain [accept Philip the Prudent; prompt on Philip]

parts.label: C
parts.question: In The Mediterranean, Braudel attacks the belief that this naval battle shifted the dynamics of maritime power in the region. The Catholic-supported Holy League won this 1571 battle against the Ottoman Empire.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This monarch brought Reginald Pole back from exile and made him Archbishop of Canterbury. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this monarch, whose marriage caused a rebellion by Thomas Wyatt the Younger. Hugh Latimer and Nicholas Ridley were among the Protestant martyrs killed during this Catholic monarch’s namesake persecution.
parts.answer: Mary I [or Bloody Mary; prompt on Mary; prompt on Marian persecutions;]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Wyatt’s Rebellion was sparked by Mary’s marriage to this prince, and later king of Spain. This king later dispatched the failed Spanish Armada against Mary’s sister Queen Elizabeth I.
parts.answer: Philip II [or Philip the Prudent; prompt on Philip; accept Felipe in place of Philip]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Latimer and Ridley were executed in this English city. A town-and-gown riot in 1209 between residents of this city’s university and its townspeople led to the creation of a rival university in Cambridge.

topics.description: Philip IV was the Habsburg king of Spain from 1621 to 1665, a patron of Diego Velázquez who ruled during the Thirty Years' War.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 1914, suffragette Mary Richardson attacked a painting by this artist with a meat cleaver. For 10  points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this Spanish artist who depicted the Infanta Margarita at the center of his 1656 canvas Las  Meninas (may-NEE-nahs).
parts.answer: Diego Velázquez [Diego Rodríguez de Silva y Velázquez]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Richardson vandalized this Velázquez painting of a nude goddess facing away from the viewer into  a mirror being held by Cupid.
parts.answer: Rokeby Venus [or The Toilet of Venus; or La Venus del espejo]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Las Meninas depicts the Infanta Margarita along with several other family members of this king,  who hired Velázquez as his court painter and led Spain during the Thirty Years' War.
parts.answer: Philip IV of Spain [or Felipe IV; prompt on Philip; prompt on Felipe]

topics.description: Henry Knox was an American Revolutionary War general, chief of artillery in the Continental Army, and the first United States Secretary of War.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This man’s relinquishment of power was compared to that of Cincinnatus, who stepped down as dictator of  Rome to go run his farm. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this first President of the U. S., who warned of the dangers of political parties and foreign entanglements  in his farewell address.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This Chief of Artillery founded the Society of the Cincinnati to preserve the ideals of the American Revolution.  A near-impregnable “Fort” named for this man is often conflated with the Bullion Depository, which holds  American gold reserves.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A president of the Society of the Cincinnati, Arthur St. Clair, presided over the issuing of an “Ordinance” named  for this adjective relative to the original 13 colonies. A fur-trading company named for this adjective competed with  the Hudson’s Bay Company until the latter got fed up and bought it.
parts.answer: Northwest [or the Northwest Ordinance; or the North West Company]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about a defunct Cabinet position, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: This member of Franklin Pierce’s cabinet later became the first and only president of the Confederate States of America.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Prior to defecting, Jefferson Davis held this now-defunct Cabinet position, which was replaced by the Secretary of Defense in 1947.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The first Secretary of War was this general of the American Revolutionary War, who crossed the Delaware River alongside George Washington.

topics.description: A federation of seven emirates on the Arabian Peninsula and Persian Gulf, including Abu Dhabi and Dubai.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Ghanaian-British architect David Adjaye designed this city's Francis A. Gregory Neighborhood  Library. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this city, where Adjaye designed a new museum building that opened in 2016 and displays  Nat Turner's Bible and the editorial desk of the Chicago Defender.
parts.answer: Washington, D.C. [or D.C.; or District of Columbia]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Adjaye's original design for the National Museum of African American History and Culture called  for this material. Auguste Rodin's The Thinker is made of this material.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Adjaye also designed the Abrahamic Family House for this country's Saadiyat Island. This country  contains the world's current tallest skyscraper.
parts.answer: United Arab Emirates [or UAE; or al-ʾImārāt al-ʿArabīyah al-Muttaḥidah] [The Burj  Khalifa in Dubai is the world's largest skyscraper.]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This country contains a man-made island chain shaped like a map of the world. An airline based in this country sponsors the soccer team Arsenal, whose stadium is named after it. Another airline in this country, Etihad, is based in its city of (*) Abu Dhabi. The world's tallest skyscraper, the Burj Khalifa, is found in, for 10 points, what country whose largest city is Dubai?
parts.answer: United Arab Emirates [or the UAE or al-ʾImārāt al-ʿArabīyah al-Muttaḥidah; prompt on Emirates]

topics.description: An Indigenous people of the southeastern United States whose sovereignty, legal rights, cultural institutions, and forced removal during the Trail of Tears are central to their history.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This tribe had a White Chief that ruled in peacetime and a Red Chief that ruled in wartime. After fighting the Red Sticks in the Battle of Horseshoe Bend, a disabled member of this tribe devised a syllabary with 86 symbols. The Phoenix newspaper catered to this tribe, whose language was made legible by (*) Sequoyah. This tribe’s chief John Ross did not approve of signing the Treaty of New Echota, which occurred after this tribe’s sovereignty was defended by Samuel Worcester in an 1832 Supreme Court case. For 10 points, name this largest of the “Five Civilized” tribes who were forced to abandon their lands in Georgia during the Trail of Tears.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After a case involving this tribe, a President apocryphally said “John Marshall has made his decision; now let  him enforce it.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this tribe, whose rights to their land were upheld in Worcester v. Georgia. This tribe was forced to  undergo the Trail of Tears.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This President declined to recognize the decision in Worcester v. Georgia. The Trail of Tears was concluded by  this President’s successor, Martin van Buren.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Andrew Jackson also opposed this tribe’s existence during a war started at the “Negro Fort.” This tribe was led  by Osceola at the Battle of Lake Okeechobee.

topics.description: The June 28, 1914 assassination of Austro-Hungarian heir Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife Sophie by Gavrilo Princip in Sarajevo, an event that helped trigger World War I.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Oskar Potiorek encouraged rioting after this event, whose participants were sentenced to death in the  Salonika Trial. One participant in this event failed to kill himself after ingesting expired cyanide and jumping  into a river 13 centimeters deep. The July Ultimatum was issued after this event, which was planned by the  (*) Black Hand and carried out by Gavrilo Princip. For 10 points, name this murder of an Austro-Hungarian  archduke, which led to the outbreak of World War I.
parts.answer: assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand [prompt on partial answer; accept reasonable equivalents,  such as the killing of Franz Ferdinand]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This event occurred after a driver made a wrong turn to a street where, according to popular legend, its perpetrator had stopped to get a sandwich. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Describe this event was perpetrated by Gavrilo Princip in Sarajevo by a Serbian nationalist group.
parts.answer: assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand [accept any obvious equivalents, prompt on but DO NOT OTHERWISE REVEAL answers like the start of World War I]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Franz Ferdinand's death sparked the beginning of this war which lasted from 1914 to 1918.
parts.answer: World War I [or the First World War, or the Great War; accept The War to End All Wars]

parts.label: C
parts.question: This country was the first to mobilize forces to support Serbia, although it withdrew from the war after a 1917 revolution deposed its king Nicholas II.

topics.description: A post-Civil War land-redistribution proposal associated with providing formerly enslaved African American families with land and a mule, especially through Sherman's Special Field Orders No. 15, and later invoked in discussions of reparations.
aliases: Forty Acres and a Mule policy

parts.label: L
parts.question: During one of this general's campaigns, railroad ties were melted and twisted into loops to render them unusable. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this US general who led a scorched-earth "March to the Sea" through Georgia during the Civil War.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Sherman's March to the Sea began with the burning of this Southern city, the capital of Georgia.

parts.label: C
parts.question: After the March to the Sea, Sherman issued Special Field Orders No. 15, which included orders to distribute land and farm animals to freed black families, as exemplified by this phrase which is often used as a slogan for slavery reparations.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This question was followed by a woman flexing her arm and saying “I have plowed, and planted, and gathered into barns, and no man could head me!” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Give this four-word question asked after describing how “nobody ever helps me into carriages or over mud-puddles” in a Sojourner Truth speech.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Truth gave her speech in Akron, Ohio, where Black workers moved during the Great Migration for jobs in this industry. Harvey Firestone founded plantations in Liberia for the raw inputs of this industry.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] After the Civil War, Truth lobbied for land grants for Blacks, which were advertised as “forty acres” and one of these animals. These horse-donkey hybrids are known for their stubbornness,
parts.answer: mules [accept Forty Acres and a Mule]
